items.desc: Stolen or gifted to France? 🇪🇬🇫🇷 Standing in the middle of Place de la Concorde is a 3,000-year-old Egyptian obelisk that originally stood at the entrance of the Temple of Luxor. In 1829, it was officially gifted to France by Muhammad Ali Pasha, the ruler of Egypt. After an incredible journey from Luxor to Paris, it was finally placed here in 1836. And this is just one of the many stories hidden behind the places you see every day 👀 Use the camera feature on the Routes app - just take a picture of what you’re seeing and discover the stories, history, and facts behind places around you💙 #exploreparis #thingstodoinparis #parisguide #placedelaconcorde #paristravel

Did you know one of Paris’s darkest legends is hidden in plain sight? 👀 Near the former Aux Vieux Marché d’Arcole, a barber and a baker were said to have worked side by side. According to the legend, customers who entered the barbershop mysteriously disappeared… while the baker next door was supposedly turning human remains into meat pies that became strangely popular. 🥧💀 Legend or not, Paris is full of stories hiding in plain sight. To discover more stories like this, download Routes app, put on your headphones, press play on Explore, and uncover the history hiding all around you -anywhere in the world. 🌍🎧 #parishistory #exploreparis #pariscafe #parishiddengems #parisguide
